chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever claims the Imamate while he is not from its rightful people, then he is a disbeliever.

key_terms.أَهْلِهَا: those rightfully qualified and entitled to it
key_terms.ادَّعَى: claimed or asserted falsely for oneself
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةَ: the divinely designated authority and leadership of the Imam
key_terms.كَافِرٌ: a disbeliever; one guilty of kufr in this context

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about someone who falsely claims the Imamate?
ai.summary: This hadith declares that falsely claiming the Imamate is an act of kufr. It underscores the creedal importance of the divinely designated authority of the rightful Imams عليهم السلام and the gravity of usurping that مقام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who claims the Imamate and he isn’t from its rightful ones, so he is an Infidel’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa fromAli ibn al-Hakam fromAban from al-Fudayl from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Whoever would claim to be the Imam and in fact he would not be the Imam he would be a unbeliever.”
